scenes.tts: How can a turkey sandwich become part of you? The bread came from wheat plants. The turkey came from a bird. Your body is made of cells too. So what are cells made of?
scenes.visual: A sandwich drawn as three labelled bars (bread: plant cells, turkey: animal cells) beside a block for your body made of cells. A question mark and the question: what are cells made of?
scenes.narration: How can a turkey sandwich become part of you? The bread came from wheat plants. The turkey came from a bird. Your body is made of cells too. So what are cells made of?

scenes.tts: Think of a necklace of beads. A monomer is a small molecule that can join to others like it. A polymer is a large molecule made of many monomers in a chain. Real chains fold, coil and branch. Their shape matters for their job.
scenes.visual: A string of small blocks. One is labelled monomer, the whole chain polymer. The chain then folds, coils and gains a branch, with the words shape matters for the job.
scenes.narration: Think of a necklace of beads. A monomer is a small molecule that can join to others like it. A polymer is a large molecule made of many monomers in a chain. Real chains fold, coil and branch. Their shape matters for their job.

scenes.tts: How does a cell link two monomers? It removes a hydrogen from one. It removes an oxygen and a hydrogen from the other. Overall, those atoms leave together as one water molecule. Joining needs energy. This joining is called dehydration synthesis. It means making something by removing water. The reverse is hydrolysis. It splits a polymer into smaller pieces by adding water.
scenes.visual: Two monomer blocks. An H chip leaves one, an O H chip leaves the other, they merge into a water chip and float away as the monomers link (dehydration synthesis). Then water returns and the link breaks (hydrolysis).

scenes.tts: Scientists sort the large molecules of life into four classes. Carbohydrates are made of simple sugars. They give quick energy. Proteins are chains of amino acids. They build tissues and run cell processes. Nucleic acids, D N A and R N A, are chains of nucleotides. They store and pass on genetic information. Lipids mostly do not mix with water. Fats, built from fatty acids and glycerol, store energy for a long time. A common fat is one glycerol joined to three fatty acids.
scenes.visual: Four rows build one by one: class name, its building blocks as a short linked chain, its main job. The lipid row ends as a glycerol block with three fatty acid bars, not a chain.
scenes.caption: Scientists sort the large molecules of life into four classes. Carbohydrates are made of simple sugars. They give quick energy. Proteins are chains of amino acids. They build tissues and run cell processes. Nucleic acids, DNA and RNA, are chains of nucleotides. They store and pass on genetic information. Lipids mostly do not mix with water. Fats, built from fatty acids and glycerol, store energy for a long time. A common fat is one glycerol joined to three fatty acids.

scenes.tts: Shape decides the job, a little like a key in a lock. Cellulose chains lie side by side in strong fibers that stiffen plant cell walls. An enzyme is usually a protein with a folded pocket where one kind of molecule fits. In D N A, two strands have bases that pair in a fixed way. A phospholipid has a head attracted to water and two tails that avoid it. In water, they form a double layer, heads out and tails in. That layer is the basic structure of the cell membrane.
scenes.visual: A notched block slides into a matching socket. Then four panels, one per class: cellulose fibers, an enzyme pocket with a fitting molecule, two DNA strands with matching bases, and a phospholipid forming a double layer.

scenes.tts: So how does a sandwich become part of you? Digestion splits large molecules into small pieces. Your cells use those pieces, along with building blocks they make themselves, to build new large molecules. A turkey protein does not become a human protein. Its amino acids are reused in new chains. Four kinds of large molecule, built from a small set of building blocks, make every part of a living thing.
scenes.visual: The sandwich splits into pieces, which join into new chains. A turkey protein breaks into blocks that rebuild in a new order as your protein. The four classes appear with their blocks under the words every part of a living thing.
